item0.title: RC_WheelLeg — 16-DOF Serial Wheel-Legged Robot
item0.desc: An open-source wheel-legged robot project from the HYNova team at Shandong Huayu University of Technology. Competed in the ROBOCON bionic legged obstacle race and won a national first prize (7th overall, top 5%). The platform is a 16-DOF serial wheel-legged robot: four wheel-legs, each with three leg joints and one drive wheel, 16 RS02 actuators in total, running on a Jetson Orin Nano 8G. The pipeline is RL training → MuJoCo simulation → Sim2Sim validation → Python Sim2Real deployment, evolving from an 8-DOF baseline into the 16-DOF hardware-validated version. The repository opens up the full mechanical design (SolidWorks / STEP), hardware, firmware, BOM, assembly documentation and the first-generation mjlab training tasks.

item1.title: 2026 NUEDC Problem H · Vehicle-Mounted Balanced Ball Control
item1.desc: A complete archive of our entry for Problem H of the 2026 National Undergraduate Electronic Design Contest (TI Cup) provincial round. The MaixCAM vision node detects the ~1 cm steel ball inside the rod groove and outputs 1-D position, velocity and confidence over a binary UART frame to an MSPM0G3507 MCU. The processing chain runs: fixed-rail ROI → LAB dark-ball candidate detection → adaptive brightness threshold → dynamic tracking window with full-rail fallback search → optional low-frequency YOLO re-acquisition → piecewise pixel-to-centimetre calibration → alpha-beta position/velocity estimation. It also includes a WebRTC video streaming and recording console, plus PC-side calibration generation and serial monitoring scripts.

item2.title: Compact Humanoid Combat Robot
item2.desc: A compact humanoid combat robot built around an RK3588 main controller. A wheeled chassis handles locomotion while the joints are driven by servos, and it can be driven three ways: web, keyboard or phone. An onboard tilt sensor detects a fallen posture and triggers self-righting, the camera on top recognizes tag codes to fire the matching action, and the entire task flow is orchestrated by a state machine.
